records.title: Kanda — navel-region energetic root
records.exact_text: While modern Western charts place the "root" at the base of the spine, classical Hatha Yoga texts (such as the Shiva Samhita, Hatha Yoga Pradipika, and Goraksha Shataka) identify the Kanda—located directly behind and slightly below the navel—as the true energetic origin of the body.
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: Kanda as an egg/bulbous root
records.exact_text: Described as shaped like a bird's egg or a bulbous root, the Kanda is the physical reflection of the Hiranyagarbha (the Cosmic Golden Egg from which the universe hatched).
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: 72,000 nadis claim
records.exact_text: All 72,000 subtle energy channels sprout directly from the Kanda in the gut, branching upward to the crown and downward to the toes like a cosmic tree (Asvattha) upside down.
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: Nabhi Marma
records.exact_text: The Nabhi Marma. In Ayurveda, the navel (Nabhi) is the primary vital hub (Marma) where Prana (life force), Agni (digestive/cosmic fire), and the circulatory systems converge.
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: Manipura — City of Jewels
records.exact_text: The solar plexus and navel center (Manipura, meaning "City of Jewels") house the internal Sun (Surya) and Agni (sacred fire).

records.title: Surya — inner Sun

records.title: Jatharagni — digestive fire
records.exact_text: Just as the physical sun burns hydrogen to sustain the solar system, Jatharagni (digestive fire) transforms raw matter into energy, consciousness, and bodily tissues.

records.title: Chandra / Bindu — head Moon

records.title: Sun–Moon alchemical cycle
records.exact_text: The Cosmic Cycle of Consumption. In ordinary life, the lunar nectar drips down from the brain and is instantly burned up by the solar fire in the gut, mirroring how time (Kala) consumes all created things. Advanced yogic practices aim to reverse or balance this solar-lunar alchemy.

records.title: Liver, spleen, gallbladder and planetary correspondences
records.exact_text: The Liver, Spleen & Gallbladder (Planetary Alchemy). In ancient medical astronomy (Jyotisha and Ayurveda), internal organs resonate with planetary forces—the gut fire aligns with Mars (Mangala, heat/transformation) and the Sun (Surya, vitality), while the watery, nutrient-storing organs align with Jupiter (Guru, expansion/metabolism) and the Moon (Soma, fluids).
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: Spine as Mount Meru
records.exact_text: The Spine (Mount Meru). Rising directly behind the gut is the spinal column, mapped as Mount Meru—the sacred cosmic axis around which the sun, moon, and constellations revolve.

records.title: Manipura inverted triangle
records.exact_text: The Inverted Triangle of Fire. Inside the ten-petaled lotus of the navel sits a downward-pointing vermilion triangle surrounded by three swastikas (ancient Vedic symbols of cosmic rotation and stability).
records.provenance: user-provided descriptive passage; not yet primary-source checked

records.title: RAM — Agni Bija
records.exact_text: The Seed Sound (RAM). The vibrational frequency of the gut is RAM (Agni Bija), the primordial sound of fire and light that ignites matter into life.

records.title: Ten petals and Sanskrit syllables
records.exact_text: The Ten Petals of Emotion and Digestion. The ten petals radiating from the gut center correspond to ten Sanskrit syllables (Dam, Dham, Nam, Tam, Tham, Dam, Dham, Nam, Pam, Pham), governing both metabolic assimilation and primal emotional drives (such as ambition, willpower, fear, and attachment).
